how: Members repeatedly call for a logo, Cairn and crest, then recruit others to complete the work.
The instruction not to get greedy explicitly limits expansion by the small size of the participating sub.
The starter role is distributed across the original logo proposal, a supplied map and a design attributed to another contributor.
Logo, Cairn and crest proposals specify the mark and include a more modest alternative.
The Cairn's reported completion supplies a construction-state report alongside its celebration.
A pixel map, an externally attributed design and an anchor coordinate make the proposed logo placeable.
Protection scripts, spare accounts and a Raspberry Pi expand placement capacity without requiring evidence of an argument about fairness.
A script user reports that it works and thanks its maker in a minimal response requesting nothing further.
Distributed proposals and a Discord-attributed design leave unseen decision-making unresolved and cannot test the global frequency claim.
Calls to protect the crest and resist the void treat placed work as something requiring repeated defence.
A participant explains attacks as random pixels on the crest while a visitor distinguishes organised expansion from other incursions.
Peace proposals, priority claims and reminders of a minimized agreed border make territorial limits a continuing topic of negotiation.
Members refuse to overwrite a cooperative neighbour and apologise for damage they intend to undo.
Restraint depends on reciprocal protection and room to complete the mark, allowing selective expansion alongside promises to spare neighbours.
Requests for neighbouring work, reports of donated pixels and promises of reciprocal filling show help moving in both directions.
Neighbouring help is explicitly limited by spare pixels and fitted around the placement timer rather than offered without regard to capacity.
Reciprocal protection and a call to protect five universities support the coalition element's smallest range without establishing a shared council or chat.
Invoking an agreement and apologising for damage do not show a dispute over who can commit all placers.
A diplomat title withdrawn as the wrong sub does not establish a member actually carrying an inter-room proposal.
Permission before drawing and a non-aggression agreement do not decide whether the mark operated as a guest under another room's host rule.
A modest alternative and a proposed crest location leave both the specified loss-trigger and a completed relocation unestablished.
The comparison with engineers defending the Cairn recruits an existing local practice into explaining canvas defence.
A school comparison and a conversion proposal do not establish a quarrel carried from before the canvas.
The school conversion call names its target but does not identify a prior rivalry as its cause, while replies invoke cooperation.
Fake news, copied styling and misleading identity replies constitute a separate April Fool performance later explicitly explained as a joke.
The concept for the close reply records procrastination, and the coded moderator clarification concerns fake news rather than containing canvas posts.
Completion announcements and expressions of pride mark collective achievements before the final close.
End announcements and the reply about lost procrastination mark closure as an event with consequences for participants.
The timelapse records the work and therefore extends the supplied theme placement beyond celebration alone.
The missed-pixel lament and recorded lettering contest retain the imperfect result beyond the identity joke alone.
Celebrating the end as OBC and expressing pride mark achievement despite the frozen error.
The request for a fixed final canvas instantiates cleanup at the stated minimum of a request without establishing completed repair or an opposing preservation debate.
Wanting the corrected canvas as a poster specifies desired reuse while leaving actual production unresolved.
A call to convert a school mark and permission for limited expansion into a flag instantiate attack proposals without proving collective execution.
A visitor's declaration of war and a later complaint about another group's alteration carry conflict in talk without establishing one unified room policy.
Calls to finish the Cairn precede its reported completion, supporting sequence without identifying which individual placements answered the call.
The starter proposal is already a recruitment call and later recruitment repeats it, so the two roles overlap in the initial turn.
Defence follows completion reporting while continued logo construction and protection also overlap.
An earlier peace proposal and later named attack calls establish both practices but do not trace defence as the cause of that negotiation.
Participants invoke an agreed border as a reason for restraint while subsequent apologies demonstrate the model's acknowledged limits on enforcing compliance.
Threat warnings receive explicit calls for defender bots and throwaways, supporting defensive automation without measuring manual insufficiency.
Completion reporting and subsequent celebration give members a finished achievement to recognise even while it remains vulnerable.
The same participant follows an OBC renaming joke with a request for a fixed final image, connecting appreciation of the result with preserving it.
Requesting a fixed final canvas for a poster links keeping a preferred record to planned reuse without establishing that either product was completed.
Design alternatives and limited capacity do not establish that a shortage after loss caused an actual move.
Treat a template as supplying a workable plan unless collective settlement is independently shown, because later redesign remains possible.
Acceptance can request enabling information before commitment, so a conditional promise must not be forced into the bare-join mechanism.
Defence and neighbouring help coexist, but the coded requests do not demonstrate that a shortage of hands caused the help exchange.
A conditional promise to preserve the neighbouring flag receives a direct reciprocal offer to fill the crest.
The attack proposal follows recruitment, but no concept states that recruiting helpers caused the turn toward attack.
The conversion proposal directly receives refusals grounded in the target's non-aggression and the existing expectation of cooperation.
An attack proposal is answered by invoking an existing working relationship rather than proposing a new treaty.
Refusal answers the school attack proposal, while the later complaint concerns another target and cannot establish a continuous attack-to-contest chain.
Joint university protection is visible but the coded calls do not establish the coalition's founding as a response to shared threats.
Recruitment and a coded procrastination reply do not show a canvas flood causing host containment.
Agreements and damage complaints do not test a transition into disputes about authority to bind other placers.
